# Erdős #242: Three unit fractions / Erdős–Straus

[All problems](../README.md) · [Lab](../../README.md) · [Progress](../../PROGRESS.md) · [Contribute](../../CONTRIBUTING.md)

**Project focus: ACTIVE.** Identify exact first denominators for strictly increasing positive three-unit-fraction representations of 4/n.

## The question

For every n>2, can 4/n be written as 1/x+1/y+1/z with strictly increasing positive integer denominators? The registered result determines the smallest first denominator only for an explicit infinite composite family.

## Read this first

The 2013 two-term fraction criterion is known. An exact scoped first-denominator family is not a general solution; present literature priority is unchecked and no Lean proof is claimed.

### Minimum first denominator on an infinite square family

All n=t², t positive divisible by 7 with every prime factor 1 modulo 3; least ordered positive first denominator equals (n+7)/4. No global conjecture solved.

Formalization: **UNFORMALIZED**. Literature: **PRIORITY_UNCHECKED**.

## Next bounded question

For prime n congruent to 1 modulo 24, can one prove an explicit residue subclass where the smallest allowed x is excluded and the next x has a symbolic positive ordered construction?

**Discriminating test:** An explicit prime n in the proposed subclass lacking the predicted x1 construction, or a correct smaller x0 witness, refutes that restricted claim. A finite prime list does not prove residue coverage.
